4| 5|# MemCore 6| 7|**Governed, Bitemporal, Local-First Memory Engine for Autonomous AI Agent Fleets** 8| 9|Capture broadly. Recall narrowly. Never trust raw conversational history. 10| 11|[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/memcore-omnix?style=flat-square&color=blue)](https://pypi.org/project/memcore-omnix/) 12|[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-blue?style=flat-square)](https://www.python.org/) 13|[![Storage](https://img.shields.io/badge/storage-SQLite_WAL_+_FTS5-07405E?style=flat-square)](#why-memcore) 14|[![Latency](https://img.shields.io/badge/latency-%3C_3ms_hybrid_recall-10b981?style=flat-square)](#sub-millisecond-hybrid-rrf-recall) 15|[![Governance](https://img.shields.io/badge/governance-Bitemporal_+_Tombstones-8b5cf6?style=flat-square)](#the-four-pillars-of-governed-memory) 16|[![Security](https://img.shields.io/badge/security-Tainted_Context_Guard-00D2FF?style=flat-square)](#tainted-context-guard-anti-poisoning) 17|[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-slate?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) 18| 19|--- 20| 21|## The Problem: State Poisoning in Ungoverned Vector Memory 22| 23|Most agent memory frameworks dump raw conversational logs directly into uncurated vector databases. Over multi-session projects, this inevitably creates three compounding failures: 24|1. **State Poisoning & Compounding Errors:** When an agent makes an incorrect guess once, that wrong guess is embedded and recalled as "truth" in all future sessions. 25|2. **Stale Code Drift:** Facts about an architecture stay frozen in memory long after the underlying files have been refactored or deleted. 26|3. **Cross-Agent Isolation Leaks:** Private agent scratchpads bleed into shared team context without hard security boundaries. 27| 28|### The Contrast: Ungoverned Vector RAG vs. MemCore 29| 30|**Ungoverned Vector Memory:** 31|```text 32|Query: "What port does the analytics service use?" 33|Recalled Chunks (Unfiltered Cosine Similarity): 34|1. [0.89] "Let's try port 8123..." (Old failed guess) 35|2. [0.87] "Runs on port 9000 in settings.py" (Stale config from last week) 36|3. [0.85] "Migrated to port 9440 with mTLS" (Actual current truth) 37|Result: ❌ Contradictory history dumped into prompt; agent guesses wrong. 38|``` 39| 40|**MemCore Governed Bitemporal Memory:** 41|```text 42|Query: "What port does the analytics service use?" 43|Recalled Canonical Memory (Hybrid FTS5 + Vector RRF): 44|1. [scope=project | lifecycle=accepted | verification=source_backed | freshness=current] 45| "Analytics service migrated to port 9440 with mTLS (settings.py)" 46| └─ supersedes: v1 ("port 9000", valid_until: 2026-10-18) 47| └─ tombstone: "port 8123" blocked (rejected claim) 48|Result: ✅ Only active canonical truth returned; SHA-256 of settings.py verified on disk. 49|``` 50| 51|--- 52| 53|## The Four Pillars of Governed Memory 54| 55|1. **Two-Zone Isolation (Untrusted vs. Authoritative):** 56| - **Zone 1: Raw Ingest Journal (`Untrusted`):** Append-only ledger recording raw user turns and tool activity. Raw journal rows are *never* recalled directly into agent prompts. 57| - **Zone 2: Canonical Governed Memory (`Authoritative`):** Only verified facts, settled architecture decisions, and explicit user rules are admitted. 58|2. **Bitemporal Versioning & Cryptographic Tombstones:** 59| - Updates (`supersede`) create immutable version chains tracking both world time and transaction time. 60| - Rejected claims leave a cryptographic **Tombstone** that permanently blocks identical bad claims from ever re-entering memory. 61|3. **Source-File SHA-256 Staleness Tracking:** 62| - Memories bound to a `source_file` automatically transition their freshness status to `stale` the instant that file's SHA-256 hash changes on disk. Unrelated Git commits leave it untouched. 63|4. **Hard SQL-Enforced Visibility Scopes:** 64| - Project-shared (`project`) and agent-private (`private`) boundaries are enforced directly in SQLite `WHERE` clauses — never in fragile Python post-filtering. Agent A can never read Agent B's private notes. 65|5. **Governed Knowledge Triples & Type-Specific Retention:** 66| - Structured `(subject, predicate, object)` triples inherit complete canonical governance: when a parent memory is superseded or tombstoned, its triples are invalidated atomically. 67| - Distinct retention policies: `constraint` memories (e.g. "never push without review") have zero decay ($\lambda = 0.0$) and high salience (1.6x), while transient `note` memories decay in days and are eligible for lossless batch compaction. 68| 69|--- 70| 71|## Sub-Millisecond Hybrid RRF Recall 72| 73|MemCore fuses lexical exactness (SQLite FTS5 BM25 with Unicode matching for technical identifiers, ports, and Thai/CJK terms) with dense vector semantics (`Xenova/multilingual-e5-small`) using Reciprocal Rank Fusion ($k=60$): 74|- **100% In-Process:** Runs directly inside Python via SQLite WAL. Zero external servers, zero Docker containers, zero open network ports. 75|- **Two-Stage 1-Bit Binary Quantization:** Compresses 384-dimensional dense vectors into 48-byte binary sign blobs. Pre-filters thousands of candidate memories using microsecond bitwise Hamming POPCOUNT before running exact float32 cosine reranking. 76|- **Salience L1 Previews:** Optional 180-character progressive summaries prioritize negations (`never`, `must not`, `ห้าม`), numerical bounds, and file paths, saving up to 80% on prompt context overhead. 77| 78|--- 79| 80|## Tainted Context Guard (Anti-Poisoning) 81| 82|Protects shared project memory against indirect prompt injection, malicious websites, and poisoned tool outputs: 83| 84|- **Untrusted I/O Tracking:** Turns that execute untrusted tools (`web_search`, `web_extract`, `browser_*`, `curl`, `wget`) are automatically stamped with `tainted: True`. 85|- **Auto-Accept Veto:** In a tainted turn, all auto-accept lanes are disabled. Both explicit durable signals (`"จำไว้ว่า..."`) and high-confidence semantic review verdicts ($\ge 0.95$) are downgraded to `candidate` status. 86|- **Consensus Requirement:** Tainted claims cannot enter `accepted` or Golden Rule status until independently corroborated by 3 distinct agents or approved by an operator. 87| 88|--- 89| 90|## One-Command Setup Wizard 91| 92|Install MemCore and run the Setup Wizard to initialize the governed database (`~/.memcore/memory.db`), configure default project bindings, and automatically register the stdio MCP server across all detected AI coding clients: 93| 94|```bash 95|pip install memcore-omnix 96|memcore install 97|``` 98| 99|`memcore install` detects and automatically registers: 100|- **Claude Code** (`~/.claude.json`) & **Claude Desktop** 101|- **Google Antigravity & Antigravity IDE** (`mcp_config.json`) 102|- **Gemini CLI** (`settings.json`) & **Codex CLI** (`config.toml`) 103|- **Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`), **Windsurf**, **VS Code (Copilot)**, **OpenCode**, and **Cline** 104| 105|Verify client registrations and database integrity anytime: 106| 107|```bash 108|memcore clients 109|memcore doctor 110|``` 111| 112|--- 113| 114|## Python SDK & MCP Tools 115| 116|### Python SDK 117| 118|```python 119|from memcore.client import MemCore 120| 121|with MemCore(project="platform", agent="hermes") as mc: 122| # 1. Store a governed fact bound to a source file for SHA-256 staleness tracking 123| mem_id = mc.remember( 124| "Analytics service migrated to port 9440 with mTLS", 125| memory_type="fact", 126| source_file="src/settings.py", 127| ) 128| 129| # 2. Hybrid recall (FTS5 BM25 + Vector RRF Fusion) 130| hits = mc.search("analytics database port") 131| for hit in hits: 132| print(f"[{hit['scope']} | {hit['verification']} | {hit['freshness']}] {hit['content']}") 133| 134| # 3. Bitemporal update (preserves immutable prior version history) 135| mc.supersede( 136| mem_id, 137| "Analytics service port updated to 9443", 138| reason="port conflict resolution", 139| ) 140|``` 141| 142|### MCP Tools Exposed 143| 144|- **`memory_remember`**: Store a governed fact, decision, preference, or note with optional `source_file` provenance. 145|- **`memory_search`**: Hybrid FTS5 + vector RRF recall with Salience L1 preview or full text. 146|- **`memory_supersede`**: Bitemporally update an existing memory while preserving immutable version history. 147|- **`memory_promote`**: Promote a private memory to shared project scope. 148|- **`memory_reject`**: Reject a memory claim and install a cryptographic tombstone refusal guard. 149|- **`memory_feedback`**: Mark recalled memories `accepted`, `rejected`, or `stale` based on actual task results. 150|- **`memory_triple_query`**: Query structured entity-relation triples governed by active parent memories. 151|- **`memory_status`**: Inspect database health, WAL mode, active memories, and governance metrics. 152| 153|--- 154| 155|## Operational CLI 156| 157|```bash 158|# Check database health, WAL mode, schema invariants, and backup readiness 159|memcore doctor 160| 161|# Store and search memories directly from shell 162|memcore remember "Python 3.10+ required for core services" --project platform --agent hermes 163|memcore search "python version" --project platform --agent hermes 164| 165|# Consolidate historical accepted memories into decision snapshots (bitemporal compaction) 166|memcore compact --project platform --days 14 167| 168|# Zero-daemon Git synchronization: export and import cryptographically sealed project snapshots 169|memcore export-project --project platform --out .memcore.jsonl 170|memcore import-project --project platform --in .memcore.jsonl 171| 172|# Create and verify atomic database backups 173|memcore backup 174|memcore backup-status 175| 176|# Export governed memory into deterministic workspace instruction files 177|memcore export # Generates workspace AGENTS.md 178|memcore export --host claude-code # Generates CLAUDE.md 179|memcore export --host gemini-cli # Generates GEMINI.md 180|``` 181| 182|--- 183| 184|## Native Hermes Agent Integration 185| 186|MemCore serves as the governed shared memory provider for Hermes Agent. The native provider adapter captures turns into the raw ingest journal, drains conversational chatter via in-process deduplication, and injects authoritative canonical memories with four-dimensional trust labels. 187| 188|Configure in Hermes `config.yaml`: 189| 190|```yaml 191|plugins: 192| enabled: [memcore] 193| entries: 194| memcore: 195| settings: 196| store_path: ~/.memcore/memory.db 197| agent_name: hermes 198| default_project: default 199| auto_join: true 200| auto_curate: true 201| 202|memory: 203| provider: memcore 204|``` 205| 206|> **Do not add `memcore/__init__.py`.** The engine root must stay a pure PEP 420 207|> namespace package so `find_spec('memcore')` never reports an `origin`; the 208|> plugin's import guard relies on that to reject a shadowing `memcore/` folder on 209|> `sys.path` and load the real checkout. `harness/test_plugin_import_guard.py` 210|> enforces this. 211| 212|--- 213| 214|## Part of the Global Agent Trinity 215| 216|Pairing **MemCore** with **trimtok** and **Skill Proof** forms the **Global Agent Trinity** — connecting all your AI coding clients to three shared local hubs without open ports or daemons: 217| 218|| Pillar | Hub | Role | 219|| :--- | :--- | :--- | 220|| **[MemCore](https://github.com/Stxyu-p/memcore)** | `~/.memcore` | **Governed Memory:** Shared bitemporal memory with hard SQL scope boundaries, source-file SHA-256 tracking, and zero hallucinated drift. | 221|| **[trimtok](https://github.com/Stxyu-p/trimtok)** | `~/.trimtok` | **Context Shield:** Cuts terminal, traceback, diff, and JSON bloat by 38–48% (real telemetry) with instant `#c1` CCR recovery. | 222|| **[Skill Proof](https://github.com/Stxyu-p/skill-proof)** | `~/.skill-proof` | **Skill Vault & Router:** Consolidates all `SKILL.md` files into one global vault and routes tasks in `< 2 ms` without LLM routing calls. | 223| 224|```bash 225|# Install and link all three tools in one pass 226|pip install memcore-omnix trimtok skill-proof-router 227|memcore install && trimtok install && skill-proof install 228|``` 229| 230|--- 231| 232|## License 233| 234|Distributed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
